title: Normal arithmetic models of an unpointed smooth connected family
statement: Let $R$ be an integrally closed integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty geometrically connected fibres, meaning that each residue-field fibre remains nonempty and connected after every field extension [def-weil-residue-field]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$, subrings $A_i\subset R$ for $i\in I$, and an index $i_0\in I$, with the following properties. Each $A_i$ is an integrally closed domain finitely generated over $\mathbf Z$ (so Noetherian); for $j\ge i$ the ring map is the inclusion $A_i\subset A_j$; and $R=\bigcup_i A_i$. Write $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, with the canonical transition maps $S_j\to S_i$. For $i\ge i_0$ there are smooth separated finitely presented morphisms $f_i:X_i\to S_i$ with nonempty geometrically connected fibres and an $S$-isomorphism $X\cong X_{i_0}\times_{S_{i_0}}S$. Here $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, and every transition $X_j\to X_i$ is the canonical base-change map [def-pc-fibre-product]. The cones $S\to S_i$ and $X\to X_i$ exhibit $S$ and $X$ as the respective scheme limits of these systems on the tail $i\ge i_0$; all their transition maps are affine, all stages are Noetherian (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]) and quasi-separated (their diagonal is quasi-compact), and every $S\to S_i$ is dominant (has dense image). The systems and their diagrams may be taken in a universe containing $R$ and $X$. No section, group structure or invertible module is assumed.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of all integrally closed finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $R$, ordered by inclusion, with $A_i=i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-finite-type-subalgebra-extension] to the prime subring to obtain a member of $I$, to the subring generated by the union of two finite generating sets to obtain a common upper bound, and to the prime subring with one element $r\in R$ adjoined to obtain a member containing $r$. These applications are legitimate because all three input subrings are finitely generated. Thus $I$ is nonempty and directed and $R=\bigcup_iA_i$. Each $A_i$ is a domain as a subring of the domain $R$. It is a set of subsets with ring operations inherited from $R$, so it is small in a universe containing $R$.

source.place: Tag 033C, lemma-normal-goes-up, third paragraph; Tag 0335 as packaged in the cited normal-subalgebra extension theorem

proof.text: The inclusions $A_i\subseteq R$ exhibit $R$ as the ring colimit: compatible maps $h_i:A_i\to B$ determine $h(r)=h_i(r)$ for any stage containing $r$; a common upper stage proves independence of this choice and preservation of sums and products. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit], $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is the scheme limit of $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. Every map $S_j\to S_i$ between these affine schemes is affine by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target], using the one-member affine cover $\{S_i\}$ of the target, whose preimage $S_j$ is affine; and these affine schemes are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Each $S_i$ is of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The generic point $(0)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ maps to $(0)$ of each $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ because $A_i\to R$ is injective; this point is dense since $A_i$ is a domain, proving dominance. A tail has the same union: given $A_i$ and $r$, take a common upper bound of $i$ and a stage containing $r$. Thus the same ring-colimit and spectrum-limit argument works on every tail.

source.place: Tag 01YW, lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine; affine spectrum of a ring colimit, also Tag 01YX

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to this nonempty directed affine-transition qcqs system and to the given finitely presented $f:X\to S$. It gives an index $a$ and a finitely presented $p_a:Y_a\to S_a$ together with an $S$-isomorphism $X\cong Y_a\times_{S_a}S$. For $b\geq a$ write $Y_b=Y_a\times_{S_a}S_b$. Base change preserves finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3); its clause (2) also makes every $Y_b$ qcqs. These are precisely the objects and cartesian squares used below.

Use [lem-sbc-affine-limit-smooth-stage] for $p_a$, its smooth pullback $f$, and the Noetherian quasi-separated system of Step 2, to get a stage $b\geq a$ where $p_b$ is smooth. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-separated] to $Y_b\to S_b$ (view the target as the identity $S_b$-scheme); the base change to $S$ is the separated $f$, and all source, target and base schemes are qcqs by Step 3. This gives $c\geq b$ with $p_c$ separated. Smoothness persists to this later stage as follows. Local finite presentation is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). A lifting problem for its base change consists of a thickening $T\subseteq T^{\prime}$ over the new base and a compatible map $T\to Y_b$. Smoothness of $p_b$, in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], supplies a lift $T^{\prime}\to Y_b$; pair it with the prescribed map $T^{\prime}\to S_c$ to obtain the required lift into the fibre product. This proves formal smoothness after base change, hence smoothness of $p_c$. The same lifting argument applies to every later base change of $p_c$.

source.place: Tag 0C0C, lemma-descend-smooth; Tag 01ZQ, lemma-descend-separated-finite-presentation; base-change lifting argument from the definition of formal smoothness

proof.text: Let $E=\{s\in S_c:n_{p_c}(s)=1\}$. This is constructible by [lem-sfb-geometric-connected-fibre-locus-constructible], since $p_c$ is finitely presented and $S_c$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-component-count-base-change], $n_{p_c}$ pulls back along $S\to S_c$ to $n_f$, which is constantly $1$ by the nonempty geometrically connected fibre hypothesis. Hence the image of $S$ lies in $E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible] to get $i_0\geq c$ such that the image of $S_i\to S_c$ lies in $E$ for every $i\geq i_0$. Apply component-count base change again: every geometric fibre of $p_i$ has exactly one connected component, so is nonempty and connected. The algebraic-closure criterion [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] then gives connectedness after every residue-field extension. In particular all fibres are nonempty geometrically connected. This argument uses no section.

source.place: Tags 055I and 055F, lemma-nr-geom-connected-components-constructible and lemma-base-change-fibres-nr-geometrically-connected-components; limits.tex Tag 05F4, lemma-limit-contained-in-constructible

proof.text: Put $X_{i_0}=Y_{i_0}$ and $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$ for $i\geq i_0$. Associating fibre products by their universal property identifies these with $Y_i$ and gives $X\cong X_{i_0}\times_{S_{i_0}}S$. Use the canonical projections for all transition maps, so composition and the displayed cartesian squares follow from the same universal property. Finite presentation persists by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), separatedness by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change], and smoothness by the explicit lifting argument of Step 4. Step 5 supplies the fibre condition. Each $X_i$ is of finite type over the Noetherian $S_i$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; it is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2). Each $X_j\to X_i$ is a base change of the affine $S_j\to S_i$, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1).

source.place: Tag 01YZ, lemma-scheme-over-limit; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-Noetherian; base-change permanence

proof.text: The cone from $X$ is a scheme limit on the tail. Indeed a compatible cone from any scheme $T$ to the $X_i$ has an $i_0$-leg $u:T\to X_{i_0}$, and composition with $X_i\to S_i$ gives a base cone. Step 2 gives a unique $v:T\to S$ for that base cone. Its $i_0$-component equals the composite of $u$ with $X_{i_0}\to S_{i_0}$. The fibre-product universal property therefore gives a unique $w:T\to X_{i_0}\times_{S_{i_0}}S=X$. At each $i$ its components in $X_{i_0}$ and $S_i$ agree with those of the given leg, hence that leg equals the projection of $w$ by uniqueness for $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$. This also proves uniqueness of $w$. All diagrams use the small set $I$ and fibre products of the given stages; enlarging the universe to contain $R$ and $X$ accommodates these choices. No extra datum on the family has been introduced.
